newsitem.title: USA: Ex-FDA Chief Kessler named dean of Yale Med School.
newsitem.headline: Ex-FDA Chief Kessler named dean of Yale Med School.

text.p: David Kessler, who led the FDA's high-profile fight against the tobacco industry, was named dean of the Yale medical school Thursday, Yale's president announced.

Kessler joined the Food and Drug Administration under President George Bush in 1990 and led President Clinton's fight against Republicans in Congress who tried to reduce its authority. He also led Clinton's campaign to regulate the sale of cigarettes to young people and to restrict advertising of tobacco products. He left the top FDA post last November.
Kessler also oversaw the introduction of Nutrition Facts food labels, improved mammography standards and cutting the time the FDA spent approving new drugs.
"I am proud and delighted to be joining one of the world's great academic medical centres," he said of his new job at Yale, which starts July 1.
Kessler, a pediatrician and a lawyer, brings "a unique array of skills and experience to the task of leading the Yale School of Medicine," Yale President Richard Levin said.

The medical school, founded in 1810, ranks fourth among American medical schools in research dollars granted by the National Institutes of Health and has an annual research budget of more than $200 million.
